course: Course 3: Programming in C and Python
audience: Complete beginners (Class 9 onwards) through college students and working engineers.
approach: Every topic is taught in C and Python side by side. C shows what the machine really does; Python shows how to get real work done quickly. Every program on every page is compiled or run by the test suite before publication, and its printed output is checked.

tiers.P1: First steps: check the idea with short, direct exercises
tiers.P2: School and college exams: Class 11-12 Computer Science and first-year programming courses
tiers.P3: Interviews and contests: coding-interview and contest problems
tiers.P4: Olympiad: Indian Computing Olympiad and IOI / ICPC style
tiers.P5: Systems and professional: university systems courses and industry practice

depth_standard: Every chapter shows each idea in C and in Python, and says exactly where the two languages differ and why.
Every program is complete, compiles without warnings (gcc -Wall -Wextra) or runs under Python 3, and its output on the page is the real output.
Every chapter explains what happens underneath: memory, the compiler or interpreter, the operating system, wherever it matters.
A problem ladder with full solutions climbs through the tiers the topic supports.
Quantum connections appear only where the programming genuinely leads there.
